title: light fluffy moroccan mirin-hon seffa
description: a light and fluffy take on the classic moroccan seffa dish, featuring mirin-hon for a slightly sweet flavor. served as a side or light meal, this dish is macrobiotic-friendly and perfect for a weeknight dinner.
instructions: heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. add the chopped onion, minced garlic, peeled and chopped carrots, and chopped celery, and sauté until the vegetables are tender. add the mirin-hon, apricot jam, cinnamon, ground ginger, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine. bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes. stir in the all-purpose flour to thicken the mixture. cook for an additional 2 minutes, or until the seffa is lightly thickened and fluffy. remove from heat and serve hot.
use a large saucepan with a heavy bottom, such as stainless steel or cast iron, to prevent scorching.
if using a saucepan with a non-stick coating, use a lower heat setting to prevent damage to the non-stick surface.
stir the mixture constantly when adding the flour to prevent lumps from forming.
if desired, add a sprinkle of cinnamon or ginger to the top of the seffa before serving for extra flavor.
seffa can be served as a side dish or light meal, and is best served immediately after cooking.
seffa will keep in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, and can be reheated in the microwave or oven before serving.
macrobiotic-friendly ingredients and cooking methods make this dish a great option for those following a macrobiotic diet.
this dish is also low in calories and fat, making it a great option for those watching their diet.
